newsitem.title: MEXICO: U.S. envoy to Mexico warns on petrochems hold-up.
newsitem.headline: U.S. envoy to Mexico warns on petrochems hold-up.

text.p: U.S. Ambassador to Mexico James Jones said Mexico could lose foreign investment because of a hold up in the sale of its petrochemical plants.

"There are many other Latin American countries...who are privatizing their energy and chemical operations and foreign investors are going there," Jones told reporters in a warning broadcast on Mexican television.

This weekend, Mexico's ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) sought to block the sale of the petrochemical plants, which has already faced stiff opposition from leftist opposition parties and unions.
Energy Ministry officials say they are studying the PRI's objections but insist the sales will go ahead.

National and international companies, including Terra and Farmland of the United States, have already placed bids for the first item on the block, a complex of ammonia plants in Cosoleacaque with annual sales of more than $400 million. The winner of that auction should have been named in April.
